LESSON: COMPOSITION OF AIR

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.2: Composition of Air

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Composition of Air. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does air pollution affect the environment?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the components of air
2. explain the effects of air pollution in the environment
3. describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment
4. appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMPOSITION OF AIR
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Composition of Air helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: COMPOSITION OF AIR
Study Composition of Air like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the components of air

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the components of air. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the components of air.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Composition of Air” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the components of air. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the effects of air pollution in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the effects of air pollution in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the effects of air pollution in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Composition of Air matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the effects of air pollution in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Composition of Air this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Composition of Air” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Composition of Air is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Composition of Air” around your school. (skill: identify the components of air)

Example 2: Say why Composition of Air matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: explain the effects of air pollution in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Composition of Air this week. (skill: describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Composition of Air” around your school. (skill: appreciate the need for clean air in day-to-day life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Composition of Air to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the components of air.
3. Practise this skill: explain the effects of air pollution in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: describe methods of reducing air pollution in the environment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Composition of Air from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Composition of Air: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Composition of Air?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does air pollution affect the environment?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Composition of Air means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the components of air.
5. Be able to: explain the effects of air pollution in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
